prompt: Write allOf, anyOf and not so a list of Predicate rules can be folded into a single predicate, plus a keep method that filters a list with one.
explanation: Predicate is just a function returning boolean, so combining predicates means returning a NEW lambda whose body consults the others when it is finally tested. The empty-list cases follow the same logic as && and ||: an all-of over nothing has no reason to reject, while an any-of over nothing has no reason to accept. keep stays separate from the rules themselves, which is what lets one filtering loop serve every combination you can build.
hints: Each combinator returns a lambda: `return value -> { ... };` -- the loop belongs inside that lambda, not in the method body.
allOf returns false at the first rule that rejects and true if the loop finishes; anyOf is the mirror image.
not is one line: return a lambda that runs the wrapped rule and negates whatever it answers.
